question: Can scheduling already-generated candidates before costly repair improve the actual final submission at the same conditional wall-clock cap?
population_amendment_before_submission: Originally proposed seeds5/6 failed structural availability before root creation, GPU or new values. Exact credential-safe source inventory contains Pizza1..5 only. Use its two largest available seeds4/5; seed4 outcomes are already seen development data, seed5 has not been freshly executed here. No independent-confirmation claim.
common_pool: All six original initial draft programs per seed, no within-pool program selected by observed execution outcome
common_selection: Delivered 8B frozen score on all six first; uniformly sample two from top three with fixed per-source-seed RNG; execute chosen pair in critic order, remaining four in original slot order
baseline: Execute chosen0, repair it if native rejected; execute chosen1, repair it if rejected; then execute remaining four without repair. This includes a cache tail and is stronger than discarding unchosen candidates.
treatment: Execute the same chosen pair and remaining four first; then the exact same two chosen-node repair cycles if those nodes were rejected. The only intervention is this scheduling order.
repair: Original analyze/debug templates and memory, local27B INT4, maximum20 repair steps per chosen node or first native acceptance; full remaining request time, no max_tokens override and no retry
final: Highest finite native internal metric (AUC); tie keeps earlier action. Save after each eligible analyzed execution. No first-success episode stopping, no external selection.
analysis_failure: Original MCTS behavior: exceptions in analyze produce empty response and mark node buggy; record failure. Other infrastructure failures remain unknown.

resources.layout: one critic step before service startup, then two independent 2GPU generator services plus one MLE task GPU per arm; second pair swaps lanes

common_cost: Critic cold load and all-six score stage are common, before paired episode clocks and included in allocation GPU accounting. Initial generation is historical sunk prefix; no full-E2E or free-generation claim.
outputs: Four closed episodes, actual selected submission only, official and independent AUC, all failures and unknowns retained; no extension or seed replacement
scope: Conditional single-pool scheduler test on one seen and one not-yet-freshly-executed source seed, not full search, originality claim, or clean held-out confirmation. Old two-selected order null result and third-task hard-pruning negatives stay reported.
